raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

On SM12x an FP8 KV cache decodes with XQA and prefills with fa2, but [#46963](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46963) sends an NVFP4 cache through fa2 for both. With speculative decoding that also costs the CUDA graphs: the multi-token verification queries no longer count as decodes, and the FlashInfer builder drops from `UNIFORM_BATCH` to `UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE`, so MTP steps run as piecewise prefills. On SM120 with TP=2 and MTP (3 tokens), a user reported on that PR about 15 tok/s decode with an NVFP4 cache; without MTP it matched FP8, and [#59791](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59791), which decodes NVFP4 with XQA, did not regress. This gives NVFP4 the decode selection FP8 already has: XQA when it can run, fa2 otherwise.

## Claims

- SM12x with an NVFP4 KV cache decodes with XQA whenever an FP8 cache would, and MTP verification steps count as decodes again under `UNIFORM_BATCH` CUDA graphs.
- Where XQA cannot run (trtllm attention disabled or a head size XQA does not take), NVFP4 decode stays on fa2 as in [#46963](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46963), through the same fallbacks FP8 uses. NVFP4 with DCP is still rejected, as before.
- SM8x and SM90 keep NVFP4 decode on fa2, as on main. SM100 behavior, prefill, and the KV writer are unchanged.

## Validation

There is no SM12x hardware here. The new test is included in an optional DGX Spark (SM121) CI step. On SM120 (TP=2, Qwen3.8-27B INT4 weights, MTP with 3 tokens), [a user reported](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60452#issuecomment-6054649551) the new test below passing (4 passed, eager and CUDA graph replay) and GSM8K through `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` at 0.962 accuracy with an NVFP4 KV cache and 0.962 with FP8, with no invalid responses in either. That report does not record the FlashInfer version or the checkout.

`test_flashinfer_xqa_nvfp4_decode_correctness` (SM12x only) writes an NVFP4 cache through the backend's writer with a full-length prefill, then decodes the last one or four tokens of each request with XQA over that cache, eager and under CUDA graph replay, at GQA 6 and head_dim 256 with K/V scales other than 1. It compares against the fa2 prefill output, which read the same cache, so NVFP4 quantization error stays out of the tolerance, and it checks that XQA is the decode kernel and that the builder reports `UNIFORM_BATCH`. It passed on SM120 in that report; on SM80 a copy without the XQA assertions passes all four cases, which only checks the cache, slot and row setup. On SM80, `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_dcp_spec_reorder.py tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py -k flashinfer` gives 29 passed, 9 skipped (the four new cases skip there), and `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer.py -k nvfp4` gives 4 passed.

XQA reading NVFP4 is covered in FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 by `test_xqa_batch_decode_nvfp4_kv`: NHD (the default layout here), head_dim 256, pages of 16 to 128 tokens, and scale factors strided apart from the data as these views are. Its only multi-token case is four query tokens per request with GQA 2 and 64-token pages, under causal and full masks; GQA 4 and 8 run single-token, and GQA 6 (the reported TP=2 setup) is not covered. Its K/V and scale addresses share the page, token and head indices, so sliding windows and HND move both together, but those, other head sizes and ragged queries are not in that test; [#59791](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59791) ran HND on SM121 and, per a report, with MTP on SM120.

## Details

The change lifts the NVFP4 exclusions added by [#46963](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46963) on SM12x only and passes the NVFP4 data and scale views to XQA:

- decode selection allows NVFP4 through the existing XQA gate on SM12x;
- `get_cudagraph_support` allows `UNIFORM_BATCH` for eligible SM12x NVFP4 groups while preserving the existing restrictions elsewhere;
- the XQA call takes `nvfp4_kv_data` and `kv_cache_sf=nvfp4_kv_block_scales` for an NVFP4 cache, the same views the fa2 path and the slot-mapping writer use.

Q stays in the model dtype and output quantization stays off (both as for FP8 on SM12x); XQA's wrapper turns `bmm1_scale`/`bmm2_scale` into its query and KV scales the same way for both dtypes. The head size 64 and attention sink refusals stay, since prefill is still fa2. The KV writer's per-append host synchronization outside CUDA graphs is a separate FlashInfer fix ([flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6204](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6204)).

---

I just tested it on SM120.
Dual 5060ti on MSI B450 with 32GB of DDR4 ram with the 2nd GPU plugged the first NVMe slot

raw_graphql_pull_request.title: [Attention] Decode an NVFP4 KV cache with XQA on SM12x

detail.body:
## Overview

On SM12x an FP8 KV cache decodes with XQA and prefills with fa2, but [#46963](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46963) sends an NVFP4 cache through fa2 for both. With speculative decoding that also costs the CUDA graphs: the multi-token verification queries no longer count as decodes, and the FlashInfer builder drops from `UNIFORM_BATCH` to `UNIFORM_SINGLE_TOKEN_DECODE`, so MTP steps run as piecewise prefills. On SM120 with TP=2 and MTP (3 tokens), a user reported on that PR about 15 tok/s decode with an NVFP4 cache; without MTP it matched FP8, and [#59791](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59791), which decodes NVFP4 with XQA, did not regress. This gives NVFP4 the decode selection FP8 already has: XQA when it can run, fa2 otherwise.

## Claims

- SM12x with an NVFP4 KV cache decodes with XQA whenever an FP8 cache would, and MTP verification steps count as decodes again under `UNIFORM_BATCH` CUDA graphs.
- Where XQA cannot run (trtllm attention disabled or a head size XQA does not take), NVFP4 decode stays on fa2 as in [#46963](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46963), through the same fallbacks FP8 uses. NVFP4 with DCP is still rejected, as before.
- SM8x and SM90 keep NVFP4 decode on fa2, as on main. SM100 behavior, prefill, and the KV writer are unchanged.

## Validation

There is no SM12x hardware here. The new test is included in an optional DGX Spark (SM121) CI step. On SM120 (TP=2, Qwen3.8-27B INT4 weights, MTP with 3 tokens), [a user reported](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/60452#issuecomment-6054649551) the new test below passing (4 passed, eager and CUDA graph replay) and GSM8K through `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py` at 0.962 accuracy with an NVFP4 KV cache and 0.962 with FP8, with no invalid responses in either. That report does not record the FlashInfer version or the checkout.

`test_flashinfer_xqa_nvfp4_decode_correctness` (SM12x only) writes an NVFP4 cache through the backend's writer with a full-length prefill, then decodes the last one or four tokens of each request with XQA over that cache, eager and under CUDA graph replay, at GQA 6 and head_dim 256 with K/V scales other than 1. It compares against the fa2 prefill output, which read the same cache, so NVFP4 quantization error stays out of the tolerance, and it checks that XQA is the decode kernel and that the builder reports `UNIFORM_BATCH`. It passed on SM120 in that report; on SM80 a copy without the XQA assertions passes all four cases, which only checks the cache, slot and row setup. On SM80, `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_flashinfer_dcp_spec_reorder.py tests/v1/attention/test_attention_backends.py -k flashinfer` gives 29 passed, 9 skipped (the four new cases skip there), and `pytest tests/kernels/attention/test_flashinfer.py -k nvfp4` gives 4 passed.

XQA reading NVFP4 is covered in FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 by `test_xqa_batch_decode_nvfp4_kv`: NHD (the default layout here), head_dim 256, pages of 16 to 128 tokens, and scale factors strided apart from the data as these views are. Its only multi-token case is four query tokens per request with GQA 2 and 64-token pages, under causal and full masks; GQA 4 and 8 run single-token, and GQA 6 (the reported TP=2 setup) is not covered. Its K/V and scale addresses share the page, token and head indices, so sliding windows and HND move both together, but those, other head sizes and ragged queries are not in that test; [#59791](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59791) ran HND on SM121 and, per a report, with MTP on SM120.

## Details

The change lifts the NVFP4 exclusions added by [#46963](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46963) on SM12x only and passes the NVFP4 data and scale views to XQA:

- decode selection allows NVFP4 through the existing XQA gate on SM12x;
- `get_cudagraph_support` allows `UNIFORM_BATCH` for eligible SM12x NVFP4 groups while preserving the existing restrictions elsewhere;
- the XQA call takes `nvfp4_kv_data` and `kv_cache_sf=nvfp4_kv_block_scales` for an NVFP4 cache, the same views the fa2 path and the slot-mapping writer use.

Q stays in the model dtype and output quantization stays off (both as for FP8 on SM12x); XQA's wrapper turns `bmm1_scale`/`bmm2_scale` into its query and KV scales the same way for both dtypes. The head size 64 and attention sink refusals stay, since prefill is still fa2. The KV writer's per-append host synchronization outside CUDA graphs is a separate FlashInfer fix ([flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6204](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/6204)).

 BACKENDS_TO_TEST = [
     AttentionBackendEnum.FLASH_ATTN,
@@ -1698,6 +1699,99 @@ def causal_mask_mod(
     )
 
 
+@pytest.mark.skipif(
+    AttentionBackendEnum.FLASHINFER not in BACKENDS_TO_TEST
+    or not current_platform.is_device_capability_family(120),
+    reason="NVFP4 XQA decode requires SM12x.",
+)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("use_cuda_graph", [False, True])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("q_len", [1, 4])
+def test_flashinfer_xqa_nvfp4_decode_correctness(
+    default_vllm_config, q_len, use_cuda_graph
+):
+    """Single-token and spec-decode queries over an NVFP4 cache decode with
+    XQA, eager and replayed, and match the fa2 prefill that wrote the cache."""
+    import unittest.mock
+
+    from vllm.v1.attention.backends import flashinfer as fi
+
+    seq_lens, bs, d = [40, 300, 1027], 16, 256
+    config = create_vllm_config(max_model_len=max(seq_lens), block_size=bs)
+    # GQA 6 at head_dim 256, as Qwen3.8-27B at TP=2.
+    config.model_config.model_arch_config = replace(
+        config.model_config.model_arch_config,
+        total_num_attention_heads=24,
+        total_num_kv_heads=4,
+        head_size=d,
+    )
+    config.cache_config.cache_dtype = "nvfp4"
+    if q_len > 1:
+        config.speculative_config = SpeculativeConfig(
+            method="ngram", num_speculative_tokens=q_len - 1
+        )
+    spec = FullAttentionSpec(
+        block_size=bs,
+        num_kv_heads=4,
+        head_size=d,
+        dtype=torch.uint8,
+        kv_quant_mode=KVQuantMode.NVFP4,
+    )
+    cg_support = fi.FlashInferMetadataBuilder.get_cudagraph_support(config, spec)
+    assert cg_support == AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_BATCH
+
+    device = torch.device(f"{DEVICE_TYPE}:0")
+    # Request i owns consecutive pages from starts[i]; page 0 stays null.
+    pages = [0] + [cdiv(s, bs) for s in seq_lens[:-1]]
+    starts = 1 + torch.tensor(pages).cumsum(0)
+    max_pages = cdiv(max(seq_lens), bs)
+    block_table = (starts[:, None] + torch.arange(max_pages)).int().to(device)
+    full_dim = nvfp4_kv_cache_full_dim(d)
+    kv_cache = torch.zeros(
+        int(starts[-1]) + max_pages, bs, 8, full_dim, dtype=torch.uint8, device=device
+    ).transpose(1, 2)
+    q, k, v = (
+        torch.randn(sum(seq_lens), h, d).bfloat16().to(device) for h in (24, 4, 4)
+    )
+
+    def run(query_lens, use_cuda_graph=False):
+        req = torch.repeat_interleave(torch.arange(3), torch.tensor(query_lens))
+        pos = torch.cat([torch.arange(s - n, s) for s, n in zip(seq_lens, query_lens)])
+        rows = pos + torch.tensor([0, *seq_lens]).cumsum(0)[req]
+        metadata = replace(
+            create_common_attn_metadata(BatchSpec(seq_lens, query_lens), bs, device),
+            block_table_tensor=block_table,
+            slot_mapping=(starts[req] * bs + pos).to(device),
+        )
+        with set_current_vllm_config(config):
+            return rows, run_attention_backend(
+                AttentionBackendEnum.FLASHINFER,
+                spec,
+                ["placeholder"],
+                config,
+                device,
+                metadata,
+                q[rows],
+                k[rows],
+                v[rows],
+                kv_cache,
+                kv_cache_dtype="nvfp4",
+                use_cuda_graph=use_cuda_graph,
+                layer_k_scale=0.02,
+                layer_v_scale=0.03,
+            )
+
+    # The full prefill writes every token through the NVFP4 writer; its fa2
+    # output for the last q_len tokens of each request is the reference.
+    _, reference = run(seq_lens)
+    xqa_fn = fi.flashinfer_xqa_batch_decode_with_kv_cache
+    with unittest.mock.patch.object(
+        fi, "flashinfer_xqa_batch_decode_with_kv_cache", wraps=xqa_fn
+    ) as xqa:

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Hi @lesj0610, thanks for the contribution. The change looks right to me: the scales go through `get_xqa_bmm1_scale` as for FP8 (no q_scale fold, since Q stays in the model dtype on SM12x), and the NVFP4 views are the same ones the fa2 path and the writer use.

1. The SM12x evidence is a single report (Qwen3.8-27B INT4, TP=2, MTP 3, "faster than fp8") with no accuracy numbers. Since the FlashInfer test does not cover multi-token NVFP4 at GQA 6 or with a sliding window, could you get a GSM8K (or similar) run with NVFP4 KV + MTP on SM12x, next to FP8 KV, plus the MTP acceptance length for both?
2. `test_flashinfer_xqa_decode_correctness` only runs a BF16 cache with single-token decode. Can it be parametrized over `nvfp4` and a `q_len_per_req > 1` batch, so the path this PR enables has a test on SM12x hardware?
3. FYI #53543 targets the same masked NVFP4 XQA decode on SM120 with a larger change and now has conflicts. It would be good to settle which one goes in.

Hi @lesj0610, thanks for adding the test and collecting the SM120 runs. LGTM. NVFP4 and FP8 match on GSM8K (0.985) and mean acceptance length (3.64 vs 3.66) in those runs, and the new test covers GQA 6, multi-token queries and graph replay with the XQA call asserted.

Minor: output throughput in that run was about 7% below FP8 (53.3 vs 57.4 tok/s) at this short context; worth rechecking once flashinfer#6204 lands.

LGTM, thanks for catching the #60620 interaction. Minor: the SM12x condition for NVFP4 XQA now lives in both the decode gate and `get_cudagraph_support`; a small shared helper would keep the two from drifting apart.
